design_decisions.physical_model: one immutable plain table per generation: kernel_fts_<digest-40> (63-byte identifier limit leaves room for the _tsv_ix GIN index suffix; SQLite keeps the historical full-digest FTS5 name) with a STORED tsvector generated under the pinned 'simple' config + GIN index, created inside the staging transaction — PostgreSQL DDL is transactional, so failed/crashed builds leave zero physical residue and no INVALID-index state exists (no CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY anywhere)
design_decisions.text_search_config: simple (lowercase, no stemming, no stop words) — closest native match to unicode61 minimalism; pinned explicitly in every to_tsvector/phraseto_tsquery call and in generation identity; deliberate documented divergence: unicode61 folds Latin diacritics, simple does not (asserted per backend)
design_decisions.identity: SQLite keeps byte-identical marker.kernel.lexical.fts5.v1; PostgreSQL generations carry marker.kernel.lexical.pg_tsvector.v1 with tokenizer pg_tsvector + config {text_search_config: simple}; identity embeds backend index id so cross-backend reuse is structurally impossible
design_decisions.query_compilation: reader takes typed logical (text, mode); PG tsquery expressions composed only from bound parameters via phraseto_tsquery (parses document text, never query grammar) — operator injection structurally impossible; FTS5 MATCH compilation moved out of context_runtime.contract into app.kernel.lexical (contract re-exports for compat)
design_decisions.ranking_contract: deterministic within-backend best-first only: FTS5 bm25 ASC vs ts_rank DESC, row_index ASC tie-break; no raw cross-backend score comparisons; neither backend uses corpus-global statistics (FTS5 bm25 per-table, ts_rank document-local) preserving high-assurance isolation
design_decisions.continuation_key: query_hash = hash of logical form (marker.lexical.query.v1 schema tag + mode + canonical tokens), backend-independent; rank stays a backend-native float with backend-owned direction; pre-PR83B2 cursors fail closed as query-binding mismatches (60s TTL makes this non-disruptive; tested)
design_decisions.retirement: DROP TABLE portable; both PG fail-closed guards and LexicalRetirementUnsupportedError removed; set/pin/staging-grace protections unchanged and proven on real PG with catalog verification
design_decisions.migrations: none required — physical artifact is runtime-managed under the already-excluded kernel_fts_ prefix on both backends; manifest columns (fts_table/tokenizer/tokenizer_config_json) already model the projection identity
